title: Transaction engine and hash-chained audit ledger
objective: Multi-entity canonical mutations happen only as validated atomic transactions: typed proposals, preconditions, dry-run, locked staged apply through the WP-200 primitives, hash-chained audit events per ADR 0010, idempotency, projection staleness handling, and recovery — with failure-injection tests.
business_value: This is the product's central trust mechanism (risk R-001): every ingestion, task, and drafting workflow mutates canonical state exclusively through this engine.
scope: Implement typed transaction-proposal domain models in src/workctx/domain/transactions.py (TXP id family, base context revision, actor/agent metadata, source references, ordered operations, pre/postconditions) aligned with schemas/transaction-proposal.schema.json, which you own and must tighten from its deliberately loose Wave 1 shape (ADR 0008 positive/negative fixtures; ADR 0011 tiers where relations are inexpressible)

Implement the engine in src/workctx/transactions/: proposal validation (structural via domain models + reference/precondition checks via the WP-220 engine's public API), deterministic dry-run reporting exact intended changes, and apply composing ONLY the WP-200/WP-201 public primitives (ContextLock with fencing; staged replace/move/delete with intent journal and bounded retries; the fenced append primitive for the ledger) per the ADR 0006 sequence

Implement the ADR 0010 audit ledger: append-only 99_meta/audit/ledger.jsonl with prev_hash/event_hash chain over ADR 0005 canonical serialization, written inside the lock after the replace sequence and before intent finalize; tighten schemas/audit-event.schema.json accordingly (event/prev hash fields, actor, operations, content hashes) with fixtures; provide chain verification and an audit_summary read API

Update the four Wave 1 workspace fixtures for transaction-proposal and audit-event (explicitly granted paths) so they validate against your tightened schemas; all other tests/workspace content stays untouched

Idempotency: applying the same proposal twice (same proposal id + base revision) is detected and refused with a recoverable conflict; interrupted applies are detectable and completable/rollbackable via the WP-200 recovery inspection API — failure-injection tests required (ADR 0006 acceptance)

Projection staleness: after a committed apply, mark/refresh the SQLite projection through its public rebuild/readiness APIs; a projection failure after canonical commit must not erase the transaction — it reports stale derived state with repair instructions (exit-band 6 semantics at the API level)

Context revision: define and maintain the base-revision token the preconditions check (document the representation in docs/reference/transactions.md); stale-revision proposals are refused with conflict semantics
Expose typed application APIs (validate_proposal, dry_run, apply, audit_summary, verify_ledger) for CLI and MCP wiring by the lead

Preconditions (D-025): compose them inside the engine — per-document validation through the domain models plus reference/existence checks through the projection query APIs over the staged in-memory set; full workspace validation via validate_workspace runs post-apply as the postcondition gate. No WP-220 changes.
Post-commit projection failure: call SQLiteProjection.invalidate() (lead-added durable mark-stale) and report stale derived state with repair instructions
non_goals: No CLI or MCP wiring (lead wires proposal/transaction commands and the ADR 0012 tools)
No artifact/inbox lifecycle (WP-310 composes your apply for archive-after-commit)
No changes to WP-200 primitives — a missing primitive capability is a coordination request to the lead, not a cross-package edit
No external writes of any kind; no LLM involvement (deterministic engine only)
deliverables: Typed proposal models with tightened schemas and ADR 0008/0011 fixtures
Transaction engine (validate, dry-run, apply, idempotency, recovery) with failure-injection tests
Hash-chained audit ledger with verification and summary APIs
acceptance_criteria: A valid multi-entity proposal applies atomically; an invalid one leaves canonical state byte-identical (verified by tree hash comparison)
Dry-run reports exact intended changes without any write, including staged content hashes
A stale base revision and a duplicate proposal id are each refused with conflict semantics

Injected failure between replaces leaves a detectable intent record; recovery completes or rolls back and the ledger reflects reality (ADR 0006 failure-injection tests, including the takeover-mid-sequence scenario)
The ledger hash chain verifies; tampering with any middle event breaks verification; the first event uses the zero prev_hash
Projection rebuild failure after commit reports stale derived state with repair instructions and does not erase the transaction
Secret-looking values are refused in proposal payloads (doc-08 control) with location-only diagnostics
security_constraints: Fictional fixtures only; the ledger records operations and hashes, never secret values or raw evidence content
All writes go through WP-200 primitives inside the context lock; no direct canonical file writes
stop_conditions: A WP-200 primitive gap (raise a coordination request; do not modify the adapter)
Any needed change to frozen files, domain files you do not own, or pyproject.toml
ADR 0006/0010 semantics that cannot be implemented as specified
